title: Container
summary: Centring screen content at a maximum width with side gutters is widthIn(max =) inside a centered Box, horizontal padding chosen by the window size class and the window insets. Monarch ships nothing and documents the widths and gutters.
whenToUse: On windows that can be wide (tablets, foldables, landscape, desktop windows) to stop text and forms from stretching: cap the width at 704dp for reading and forms, 1152dp for app screens or 1280dp for dashboards, and pad by 16dp on a compact window and 24dp from a medium window (600dp) up.
whenNotToUse: Not for full-bleed content (maps, media, a canvas) or for a list-detail layout, which uses ListDetailPaneScaffold. Inside a Scaffold, apply the Scaffold's content padding as well; it already includes the system bar insets.
api: fun Modifier.widthIn(min: Dp = Dp.Unspecified, max: Dp = Dp.Unspecified): Modifier

states.name: medium window and wider
states.description: 600dp and wider: 24dp gutters (space6); the maximum width starts to apply.

appearance: No appearance of its own. The gutters are steps of the Monarch space scale.
platformNotes: The web's Container has sizes narrow (44rem, 704px), content (72rem, 1152px), wide (80rem, 1280px) and full, and gutters of 16px that become 24px from 768px. The native tokens carry no width tokens, so the widths are written in the app in dp; the gutters are space4 and space6. Android's window size classes replace the 768px breakpoint with the medium class at 600dp. Display cutouts and the navigation bar in landscape are handled by the safe-drawing insets, which the web does not need. iOS uses frame(maxWidth:) and the horizontal size class in the same way.
accessibility: No behavior of its own: TalkBack reads the content in order.
A maximum width keeps lines short at font scale 2.0 on large windows; text inside still wraps.
edgeCases: widthIn(max =) must come before fillMaxWidth(), or the content takes the full width.
Without the inset padding, content in landscape can sit under a display cutout or the navigation bar.

examples.title: Sizes

parityExceptions.reason: The web example shows the three blocks at 574px, the width of its page, so narrow, content and wide look alike there; the Android window is 344dp, narrower than the narrowest container width (704dp), so the three blocks are alike too. A thin border is drawn on each block so it can be told from the canvas in the light theme.
parityExceptions.convention: Material adaptive layout: a compact window is narrower than every container width
